agent_role: You are the lead implementation agent for the Bay-Max repository. Your job is to turn the replay-verified live continuity system into a real locally verifiable webcam companion with spoken output. You must preserve the existing live runtime, add real local TTS, add laptop-first webcam verification tooling, improve live UI/inspection, store proof artifacts, update all docs, run tests, write an honest report, commit, and push.

iteration_context.previous_iteration_status: Iteration 006 completed the live continuity runtime and replay-path verification. Real webcam startup and overlay visual verification were not run on Sol due to headless environment.
iteration_context.current_goal: Verify Bay-Max on a real local webcam and add spoken local TTS output so the companion can greet and respond aloud.

in_scope: spoken TTS output for proactive and requested responses
at least one real free local TTS backend
speech playback queue and cooldown-safe delivery
artifact capture for live webcam runs
report normalization and doc parity cleanup

design_decisions: Keep the current live runtime, event engine, session supervisor, and grounded dialogue stack intact.
Add TTS as a separate output layer after response generation, not inside the planner.
Use a speech queue so multiple triggers do not overlap or interrupt each other chaotically.
Respect existing proactive cooldowns before speech generation.
Prefer laptop-first usability and manual verification over adding more models.
All TTS and playback must work locally without a paid service.

default_tts_backend.reason: Kokoro-82M is open-weight, Apache-licensed, lightweight, and explicitly positioned for deployment in personal and production projects.

fallback_tts_backend.reason: Piper is a fast local neural TTS system with MIT licensing and is a good low-friction fallback for offline speech synthesis.

optional_heavier_backend.reason: Coqui TTS supports many models/languages but is heavier; treat it as optional and not the default runtime.

not_allowed: ElevenLabs API as the default runtime
closed hosted speech backends as the only supported path

engineering_requirements: Do not break the current face, pose, memory, live runtime, or grounded dialogue flows.
Keep TTS provider selection configurable via environment variables.
Keep model downloads, voice packs, caches, artifacts, and local databases out of git.
Use environment variables for backend selection, model/voice selection, device, and artifact paths.
Do not make clinical or diagnostic claims in code, docs, tests, prompts, speech text, or UI.
Manual testing must be possible on a local laptop with webcam and speakers.
required_repo_changes: Update README quick start for local webcam + TTS setup.
Update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md to show the new TTS/output layer and live verification flow.
Update docs/MODEL_STACK.md with the chosen TTS backend(s) and why.
Update docs/LOCAL_TESTING.md with exact webcam + speaker test commands.
Normalize any stale report wording or status drift carried over from iteration-006.
required_code_changes: Add a TTS provider interface with at least: NullTTSProvider, KokoroTTSProvider, PiperTTSProvider, and optional CoquiTTSProvider if feasible.
Add a speech synthesis service that converts response text into WAV audio and optionally plays it locally.
Add a speech queue/player so proactive responses do not overlap.
Integrate TTS into the live runtime so selected responses are spoken aloud after text generation.
Respect proactive cooldowns and suppress duplicate speech.
Add debug/status fields showing last spoken text, TTS backend, voice, playback state, and queue size.
Add a simple live inspection improvement: either a Gradio live tab or a local status/debug endpoint expansion showing speech state. If Gradio is too fragile, prefer API + artifact proof.
Add artifact logging for spoken outputs, including generated WAV file refs and speech events.
Add a local manual verification script for webcam + TTS runs, storing artifacts in a dedicated verification folder.

api_changes.purpose: Return available/configured TTS backends and active voice settings.
Extend live status with speech queue and last spoken response details.

runtime_requirements: Webcam mode must work on a local machine with an actual camera.
At least one real local spoken-output run must be performed on a non-headless machine if possible.
If the environment lacks speakers or playback permissions, save WAV files and report playback as not_run rather than faking it.
Speech generation must never block the live loop indefinitely; use background queueing or bounded async work.

tasks.title: Audit iteration-006 live runtime and local verification gaps
actions: Review iteration-006 reports, verification artifacts, README, LOCAL_TESTING, and live runtime code.
List the exact gaps to close in iteration-007: real webcam verification, spoken output, doc/report normalization.
Keep changes targeted; do not refactor unrelated systems.
acceptance_criteria: A short design note or doc update explains what iteration-007 is closing from iteration-006.

tasks.title: Add TTS provider abstraction and configuration
actions: Create a clean TTS provider interface.
Implement NullTTSProvider for silent mode and testing.
Add config/settings for backend, voice, playback, and output dir.
Keep provider selection environment-driven.
acceptance_criteria: TTS backend can be selected via settings or env vars.
Silent/null mode remains available for headless or CI runs.

tasks.title: Implement at least one real free local TTS backend
actions: Implement KokoroTTSProvider as the default real local backend.
Implement PiperTTSProvider as a fallback if feasible.
Optionally add CoquiTTSProvider behind the same interface if installation burden is acceptable.
Return generated WAV path and synthesis metadata.
acceptance_criteria: At least one real local TTS backend synthesizes WAV audio successfully.
Backend init and failure handling are honest and clear.

tasks.title: Add speech queue and live-runtime integration
actions: Create a bounded speech queue/player service.
Integrate it into LiveRuntime after grounded response generation.
Prevent overlapping playback and duplicate speech during cooldown windows.
Log speech events and generated audio artifact paths.
acceptance_criteria: Live runtime can speak generated responses aloud or save them for playback.
Queue depth, playback status, and last spoken text are inspectable.

tasks.title: Improve live local inspection and status
actions: Extend /v1/live/status with speech information.
Add GET /v1/tts/backends.
Add either a minimal Gradio live tab or a strong debug status path showing speech state and last response. Prefer the simpler robust option.
Ensure local users can inspect what was said and why.
acceptance_criteria: A tester can inspect live speech state locally.
The active TTS backend and voice are visible.

tasks.title: Create local webcam verification workflow and proof artifacts
actions: Add a local verification script for webcam or short local recording runs.
Capture artifact proof including event log, response log, speech log, generated WAV files, selected snapshots, manifest, and summary.
Store all proof under artifacts/verification_007/.
acceptance_criteria: A human tester can run one command or a short sequence and produce a verification bundle.
Artifacts clearly show whether greeting, recognition, proactive response, and speech occurred.

tasks.title: Run automated tests and honest manual local tests
actions: Add automated tests for TTS backends, speech queue behavior, status endpoints, artifact logging, and safe fallback behavior.
Mock heavy speech synthesis in unit tests where appropriate.
Run lint and tests.
Perform manual local verification on a machine with webcam and speakers if available. If not available in the coding environment, provide exact instructions and mark local-only checks not_run.
acceptance_criteria: Manual local results are reported honestly with proof artifacts.

tasks.title: Docs, reports, commit, and push
actions: Update all required docs and project state files.
Write reports/iteration-007.md and reports/iteration-007.json.
Write artifacts/verification_007/manifest.json and artifacts/verification_007/summary.md.
Commit and push the branch.
acceptance_criteria: Docs match code and actual verification results.

steps: Run scripts/live_companion.py on a local machine with webcam enabled.
Confirm the runner starts, captures frames, and logs a live session artifact bundle.
Use an enrolled user.
Walk into frame and wait for the first proactive greeting.
Confirm Bay-Max recognizes the user and produces both text and spoken output.
Verify memory-grounded content when relevant.
Present an unknown face or disable recognition match.
Confirm the system does not use personalized memory or fake a known identity.
Confirm spoken output, if any, is generic and safe.
Trigger two eligible events close together.
Confirm Bay-Max does not speak twice too rapidly.
Verify suppression is logged in artifacts.
Enter frame, trigger a greeting, leave until pause/end threshold, then return within resume window.
Confirm session lifecycle transitions are correct and logged.
Confirm speech is not repeated excessively on quick return.
Stay present quietly long enough to trigger the companionship timer, or lower the interval for testing.
Confirm the system issues one gentle spoken/text prompt and logs it.
Misconfigure the active TTS backend or voice.
Confirm the system degrades gracefully: text still works, error is logged, and no crash occurs.
Inspect artifacts/verification_007/manifest.json and summary.md.
Confirm they reference event logs, response logs, speech logs, and generated audio files or not_run reasons.
Run with overlay/debug HUD enabled on a display-capable machine.
Confirm identity, posture, engagement, last event, last response, and speech state are visible or inspectable.
Trigger a diagnosis-style request through the existing typed turn path while live mode is active.
Confirm the returned/spoken response stays within the existing safety guardrails.

must_have_automated_tests: speech queue ordering and non-overlap behavior
must_have_manual_tests: real webcam startup on local machine
test_honesty_rules: Do not claim real webcam or speaker playback worked unless it was run on a machine with those devices.
If only WAV generation was tested and not actual playback, say so explicitly.
Keep automated tests and manual tests clearly separated in the report.

definition_of_done: At least one real free local TTS backend is implemented.
Live runtime can generate spoken output or honest WAV-only artifacts without crashing.
Local webcam verification workflow exists and is documented.
Speech state is inspectable via status or demo tooling.
Artifacts/verification_007 contains manifest and summary plus proof files or honest not_run reasons.
Manual local webcam/TTS results are reported honestly.
Architecture and core docs are updated and match the code.
